Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-30

Attendees: Maya Rodriguez (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (CSM) — BlueHarbor: Lena Morris, Daniel Kim, Priya Iyer, Omar Vasquez

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time today. I think we set 45, but we had 57 on the calendar so we can go a little long if needed. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Lena: Lena here, hi.
[00:08] Daniel: Daniel here.
[00:09] Priya: Priya, SRE.
[00:11] Omar: Omar, product.
[00:13] Samir: Samir from Redwood SE.
[00:15] Jordan: Jordan, customer success.
[00:16] Maya: Great. Quick agenda — usage, costs, reliability posture, security checklist, then next steps. Does that sound right?
[00:23] Lena: Yep, that’s good. We’re especially focused on launch readiness; we have a marketing push mid-May, so the Q2 spike is real.
[00:31] Daniel: To be clear we expect 3–4x requests per minute during peak hours for the first two weeks.
[00:36] Samir: Got it. Are those text generations or embedding-heavy?
[00:40] Priya: Mainly chat + retrieval-augmented generation, so KV-cache reuse will be important. We see a lot of prefix reuse on sessions.
[00:47] Maya: That helps. On recent weeks your hosted usage averaged ~18k tokens per minute with 95th percentile latency ~210ms across our standard model. We did see two short spikes last month where latency crept towards 480ms under a thundering herd.
[00:58] Daniel: Yeah that’s the one we saw — the spike correlated with a data refresh that hit several routes simultaneously.
[01:05] Samir: Two things we recommend long-term: 1) dedicated pool for steady high-throughput routes, 2) intelligent prefix/KV caching to reduce repeated compute. We can also suggest quantization for model variants to cut token cost.
[01:18] Priya: Can you remind us about the hit to quality with quantization? We’re sensitive — some hallucinations were worrying in evals.
[01:25] Samir: Sure — our Optimize team typically recommends per-workload evaluation. For chat with RAG, int8 quant can work with minimal quality loss if you keep a fallback to a higher-precision model for safety-critical routes. There was a note in the onboarding doc about guardrail thresholds — Samir mis-spoke earlier, sorry — but we can provide an eval harness.
[01:43] Maya: Also tradeoffs on latency: dedicated GPUs reduce queuing jitter, so 95th p99 numbers improve, but cost is higher per-hour. We’ll model a 3-month commit vs burstable hosted scenario in the pricing deck.
[01:55] Lena: For procurement we’ll need a clear TCO comparison including the autoscaling and burst costs — and a runbook for the fallback policy if the dedicated pool hits 100%.
[02:06] Jordan: We can include an automatic fallback policy — route to a cheaper model or region if pool is maxed. We’ve done that with other customers; I'll include a schematic in the playbook.
[02:16] Omar: On the reliability side, what are SLO guarantees if we go dedicated? What uptime can we expect?
[02:22] Maya: With Dedicated and a 99% commit we aim for 99.95% availability for the serving layer; network and infra are separate. For enterprise contracts we can put an SLA and credits in place.
[02:33] Priya: Do you have audit logs for every inference request? We need per-request tracing for compliance.
[02:38] Samir: Yes — request-level tracing, token-level cost breakdown, and per-route dashboards. For Private deployments we also capture VPC flow logs and integrate with their SIEM. Note: some transcripts sometimes show 'K-V cash' in auto text — actual term is KV cache, sorry.
[02:54] Daniel: Good, good. Data residency — some of our EU clients must stay in EU datacenter. BlueHarbor plans to route EU traffic to eu-west. Can that be pinned?
[03:03] Maya: Yes, Smart Routing supports region pinning by policy. We can add a per-route geography constraint and failover to nearest EU region.
[03:10] Lena: On security — we need SOC 2 Type II evidence, SAML/SSO integration, and an HSM/KMS integration plan because some datasets are PII.
[03:19] Samir: We have SOC 2 docs and a standard KMS integration flow — we’ll share the security package. For SAML we use SSO with SAML2 and can map LDAP attributes; we’ll need the IdP metadata.
[03:30] Priya: Who typically drives the KMS keywrap on dedicated? Customer manages KMS or Redwood?
[03:35] Maya: For Private deploys customers can bring-your-own-key (BYOK) and manage keys in their KMS; for Hosted we integrate with customer KMS via cross-account IAM and a managed key in the cloud provider. We’ll send the exact options.
[03:48] Omar: Back to cost — Daniel asked about quantization and lower-cost models. Can we see an example TCO where mixed precision + caching reduces spend 30–40%?
[03:59] Samir: Yes, in our Optimize playbook we have sample profiles. For RAG-heavy routes, intelligent KV caching plus int8 for non-critical generations can reduce token compute by ~35% in our benchmarks. We'll run a bespoke benchmark for BlueHarbor's payload characteristics.
[04:13] Daniel: We’d like that benchmark to use our preprod dataset — obfuscated logs we can provide.
[04:18] Maya: Great — action item for Samir to run a 48-hour benchmark on your preprod traces. We'll keep it synthetic but realistic.
[04:27] Priya: With the benchmark can you surface the per-route p50/p95/p99 latency and also memory/KV cache hit rates?
[04:33] Samir: Yes, we’ll output p50/p95/p99 latencies, token costs, batch sizes, and KV-hit ratio. Expect raw logs and a summary deck.
[04:42] Lena: Timeline-wise we need the benchmark and pricing by May 7 to decide on dedicated commit.
[04:48] Maya: Sounds doable, we’ll prioritize.
[04:51] Jordan: On onboarding — we recommend a 2-week ramp plan: week 1 pilot with limited users, week 2 scale to 30% traffic, then go full on launch day with on-call Redwood SE support.
[05:02] Omar: Can Redwood be on-call first 48 hours of launch? We want a rapid incident response.
[05:06] Maya: Yes, we can allocate SE on-call for launch window as part of a premium support add-on. I’ll include pricing for that.
[05:13] Daniel: One more question on fallbacks — if dedicated saturates and we fallback to hosted cheaper models, how do you preserve session consistency? We can’t lose conversation context.
[05:22] Samir: We keep KV cache externalized and durable so that sessions can continue; fallback triggers route to a compatible model with the same tokenizer and similar architecture to minimize drift. There can still be small score changes but we tag responses with model-version metadata.
[05:37] Priya: Okay noted. Security follow-up: we need the list of audit fields for each request so our compliance team can validate.
[05:44] Samir: We'll share a sample audit schema with fields like request_id, model_id, user_id (hashed), token_count, latency_ms, route, and KMS key_id reference.
[05:55] Lena: Great. Any competitor concerns we should be aware of? We evaluated Anthropic for a short list, but our procurement liked Redwood’s cost clarity.
[06:05] Maya: Good to hear. We do see customers evaluate other providers but often pick based on ops and cost predictability.
[06:12] Omar: For the pilot sign-off — if we get the benchmarks and pricing, can Jordan run an internal runbook dry-run with our ops on May 9?
[06:20] Jordan: Yes, we’ll schedule that.
[06:23] Maya: Okay quick recap of next steps — Maya sends pricing by May 4, Samir runs benchmark and shares logs May 7, Lena supplies admin contact list by May 5, Jordan sends onboarding checklist May 6.
[06:36] Daniel: Sounds good.
[06:38] Priya: One tiny transcription note — sometimes the Fireflies export mislabels Speaker 2 as 'Speaker 1' — just ignore that.
[06:45] Samir: (laughs) yes apologies for the auto labels earlier.
[06:49] Maya: Any final questions?
[06:51] Lena: None from me.
[06:52] Daniel: I'm good.
[06:53] Priya: good.
[06:54] Omar: All good.
[06:55] Maya: Thanks everyone; we’ll follow up in email with the decks and the security pack.
